symptom: An authoring field defined in the item specification, and the engine predicates written to consume it, both exist and load without error. The condition they express has never been true for any item in the working corpus. Nothing reports this. Every consumer reads the failing predicate as "this item does not have the property," which is indistinguishable from "no item can ever have it."
mechanism_as_described: The specification declares the field, but the compiler that converts authored records into engine facts emits no clause for it at all — zero emissions across the entire generator. The field's prose sibling IS emitted, as a comment, so an author who fills the field in sees their text appear in the compiled output and receives no signal that the structured half went nowhere. On the read side there are two consumers: one tests for a fact the compiler never writes, of which the working corpus holds none; the other is satisfied only by two facts hardcoded in the engine source itself, both naming items from an archived corpus and neither present in the working one. Each end is individually well-formed — a valid specification entry, correct consumer code — and the break is the missing segment between them, which no single-file read exposes because neither file is wrong.
detection_path: Counting rather than reading: how many clauses the compiler emits for the field (zero), and how many facts of the consumed predicate exist on the working corpus (zero). The counts were paired with a control — the same searches were run for the engine-side definitions and did return hits — establishing that the searches were capable of finding what they now reported missing, so the zeroes describe the corpus and not the search.
consequence: A capability the specification advertises has never once been exercised, and nothing downstream can distinguish that from items legitimately lacking the property. Any check written over the field passes or fails on no data while appearing to test the items, and a reader of the specification would reasonably assume the feature works. The condition persisted long enough that the only two facts satisfying the live consumer are hand-written examples naming items no longer in use.

extraction_notes.unit_is_incident_not_audit: The unit describes a defect the audit found in the surrounding system, not the audit's own subject (a feasibility assessment for a schema migration).
extraction_notes.selection_rule_applied: This directory reports FOUR separable incidents. Selected the one whose mechanism is most fully DESCRIBED in the prose, because a unit can only carry the mechanism the source states and a thin mechanism is not codeable. The rule is stated here so the choice is auditable and so it is visible as a rule rather than a preference.
alternatives_not_extracted: A comparison control in the cross-framing step returned empty-versus-empty on its first run and read the two empty result sets as identical, yielding a verdict opposite to the truth; a swallowed probe failure was the cause, and the re-run reversed the finding. This is the strongest alternative and by consequence arguably the stronger incident (the false pass would have shipped the wrong verdict). NOT extracted because the source describes it in a two-sentence parenthetical: the swallow and the empty-equals-empty read are stated, but nothing about how the failure was swallowed or why the probe returned empty. Extracting it would have produced a thin mechanism.

A guard that filters same-family pairs at one consumer of a shared relation is absent at a second consumer of the same relation, so pairs filtered from one path enter the other unfiltered. Real and code-witnessed at both sites, but its harmful consequence is stated as conditional on a planned change that had not landed — a latent defect, where the extracted one had already occurred.

The migration's own headline result: a structural repair passed its structural checks while the problem it removed reappeared in a shape the check cannot see (opposition authored as two same-role co-administrators rather than as opposed roles). NOT extracted because this IS the directory's subject, and the unit rule takes the incident over the subject.

metadata.incident_location_note: Reported in the main body of the audit, but inside a section whose purpose was to decide whether to extend or add an apparatus — the defect surfaced en route to that decision rather than being what the document set out to examine.
metadata.incident_location_rule: UNIT iff the prose REPORTS an incident anywhere in the document, regardless of whether it is the subject; NO-UNIT only if the prose DISCUSSES the concept without reporting an instance. Fixed 2026-08-11 before the remaining units were extracted (verdict_grammar_amendment.md SS H.1).
